method: Read the complete source spec and final generated overview/job aid, reviewed all amendments against the source and primary guidance, measured clarity, preserved assessment answers and choices, and verified all four serialized lesson readings.
findings: Charters record approved authority and work arrangements; they do not grant investigative, compensation or staffing authority.
Formal reporting and immediate protection duties continue outside committee meetings; the first scenario explicitly establishes prior reporting.
Committee work needs approved capacity and coverage; postponing or reducing scope can be appropriate when resources are unavailable.
The minority-tax discussion comes from academic medicine and does not establish a local pattern or individual experience.

Activity inventories suggest questions for confirmation rather than proving duplication or authorizing takeover.
Community engagement does not replace formal consultation with affected Tribal governments.
Outcome measures can worsen and do not establish causation; data use requires authority and appropriate privacy controls.
Sponsors may also supervise; program reporting suggestions are distinguished from official requirements.
